items.title: Karl Berger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014
items.q: When you look at scores that Bach wrote, he didn’t write within bar lines.

ctx.x: As a schooled musician, can you do that on purpose?

Yeah, of course, yeah. You have to learn what we call beat-for-beat attention. This is our training that we do with the Creative Music Studio. I call it beat-for-beat attention. That means each beat has the same attention. So you’re not going for like one — and that’s more important than the two or the four. The four is as important as the one. And if you go for each beat, all of a sudden there’s no need for a bar line. Because you are there. So once you’re there you don’t need to know it’s four or it’s five. You…
hear bar lines. When you hear bar lines then there’s something wrong with the music. It’s not really well assimilated.
